page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e3.xlarge is an x86_64 virtual machine based on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, featuring 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. Compute resources are provisioned via dedicated CPU allocation, accompanied by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set support includes AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and standard integer extensions such as BMI2 and FMA.

The instance delivers a memory-heavy configuration, providing 64.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs included. In addition, no local storage is bundled with the instance, requiring network-attached storage solutions for all non-volatile persistence. Zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are supplied.

Benchmark results demonstrate mixed performance characteristics. In compute assessments, multi-core operations perform at an average tier, recording 8825.18 on stress-ng multi-core and 10041.11 on PassMark CPU. Conversely, single-threaded throughput falls in lower ranges, with stress-ng single-core scoring 1109.08 and single-threaded gzip compression achieving 19.15 GB/sec. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth registers 60.77 GB/sec for reads and 49.44 GB/sec for writes. The PassMark database operations benchmark scored 2206.06, while Redis SET operations achieved 11.0 million operations per second.

With an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the server provides substantial memory density per core, though older generation per-core throughput represents a clear tradeoff against newer compute-focused families. The instance is suited for caching layers, in-memory processing, enterprise middleware, and general multi-threaded applications that demand generous memory space rather than extreme single-thread speed.
